newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra not worried by P&G's Helidac.
newsitem.headline: Astra not worried by P&G's Helidac.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co's new drug Helidac could take a slice of the enormous U.S. gastric ulcer market but poses no threat to the Astra drug Losec, the Swedish drugs company on Wednesday.
Astra company spokesman Staffan Ternby said the company still expected Losec to become the biggest selling drug in the U.S. in 1997.
"Helidac is a combination treatment with three different agents and the only advantage is that all three are proven and cheap," Ternby told Reuters.
He said Helidac can certainly break Helicobacter Pylori, the bacteria that is thought to be the cause of gastric ulcers, but it does not heal gastric ulcers.
"We are talking about a completely different division (Helidac compared to Losec)...Procter & Gamble will certainly be able to sell on this enormous market but it does not worry us," Ternby said.
Ternby forecast continuing strong sales development for Losec in the U.S..
"There is no reason for this to change dramatically. Even in the U.S. Losec will soon be the country's biggest selling drug. I would not be surprised if this happens in 1997," he said.
